findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of a tuple, which is unstable across processes
findings.body: The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash() for ints is stable, but the key is also not tied to the allowlist value; more importantly the cache stores only the boolean eligibility per project set for 60s, so an allowlist change is ignored for up to 60 seconds while the code comment claims this is safe. invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called, so the advertised invalidation on allowlist change does not happen. Also the cached value is the allowlist check only, so a cached True for an organization is reused regardless of allowlist changes.

findings.title: Cache hit short-circuits on falsy check incorrectly typed; cache.get returns non-bool values
findings.body: cached_result is compared with `is not None` and returned via `cached_result and ...`. If the cached value is False, the function returns False, which is correct, but the return type is not guaranteed to be bool when cached_result is a non-bool stored by another writer under the same key. Under mypy this is also an untyped cache value returned as bool.

findings.title: Membership test is O(n*m) on a list read from options
findings.body: `project_id in allowlist` performs a linear scan of the allowlist for each project, and the allowlist is a list from options. For large allowlists and many projects this is quadratic per request. Converting to a set once would be the expected approach given the stated performance goal.

findings.title: upsampled_count returns sum of sample_weight over all rows, ignoring the upsampling eligibility and null weights
findings.body: The new function sums sample_weight with no null handling or filter; events lacking sample_weight (for example non-allowlisted projects mixed into the same query, or events stored before the feature) will contribute null/zero and silently undercount. The comment asserts the schema guarantees the column for all events, but the endpoint does not verify this beyond the allowlist check. The result also silently changes the metric name the user requested (count() is returned aliased as count), which can break clients that expect the column type.

findings.title: Error message text changed without need
findings.body: The validation message was changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is an unrelated user-facing API response change bundled into the upsampling PR, and it can break clients matching on the string.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is recomputed for every _get_event_stats call, including per-widget split queries
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called at the top of _get_event_stats, which runs up to four times per request in the dashboard split path. Each call hits the cache and option lookup again; the comment claiming a 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' is misleading since the decision is recomputed each time and can differ between calls within one request if the cache expires or the allowlist changes mid-request.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace and redundant variable aliasing
findings.body: Lines with only whitespace after the upsampling check (and the duplicated `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` alias) add noise. The comments describe 'late transformation' and 'caching' that do not match the code, which is misleading to maintainers.

findings.title: Upsampling is only applied to the query columns in some branches; top-events and RPC paths compute final_columns but the non-top-events path reassigns it inconsistently
findings.body: In the RPC branch the transformation at line 277 reruns from query_columns, discarding nothing, but in the top_events branch final_columns is only transformed when upsampling is enabled and then passed as timeseries_columns while selected_columns still uses raw fields. Count() is rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count' but the top-events path also passes the alias string into the equation/orderby machinery that expects the raw function name, so orderby on count() can fail or sort incorrectly. Behavior differs between the top-events and standard branches with no test coverage for top-events.

findings.title: Test factory silently overwrites sample_rate from contexts for every stored event
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is applied to every event stored through the shared store_event factory, and it swallows all exceptions. This changes the sample_rate of all test events that carry error_sampling contexts globally, affecting unrelated tests and hiding malformed data instead of failing.

findings.title: Test setUp overwrites self.user and self.user2 after login, and assertions expect counts of 10 that the stored data cannot produce
findings.body: setUp logs in self.user then reassigns self.user to a new user, and the tests assert count==10 for allowlisted projects while only one event per project per bucket is stored; the expected upsampled value depends on client_sample_rate 0.1 being applied through sample_weight, which the test never verifies. The transaction test also asserts counts for a dataset the feature should not touch, and the assertions rely on unverified behavior, so these tests are likely to be wrong or flaky.

findings.title: Unit tests do not cover the cache path or the invalidation function
findings.body: The tests cover the pure helpers but not is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, its cache behavior, or invalidate_upsampling_cache. The stale-cache behavior described above (60s staleness after allowlist change) is therefore untested, and the unused snuba_params/organization fixture data is never exercised.

findings.title: Test module added to strict typing list without matching sentry-repo change being justified
findings.body: The pyproject.toml change adds the new helper and test module to the strict mypy override list, but the helper's dependency on untyped Any for dataset and the local imports inside _should_apply_sample_weight_transform make this strictness claim unverified. Additionally a stray submodule pointer file 'sentry-repo' is added at the repository root, which is unrelated to the feature and should not be merged.
